passage:
Sunday night
Third pottery class today. My bowl collapsed twice and I laughed so hard with Tsering that the teacher had to shush us. 🙂 Didn't check my phone for two whole hours. That's new. Mum says I'm a calmer girl these days.
Sahil picked me up after and told me about his day without me asking, including lunch with his team. Old me would have asked who sat where. Today I just listened. It helps that he's the same every day, calls when he says he'll call.
I still get the tight chest sometimes. Thursday is my second session with the campus counsellor. She says the feeling can shrink when my life has more in it than him.
I think she's right. My bowl is drying on the windowsill.
— Dolma

qa.q: What did Dolma make at pottery class?
qa.a: She made a bowl, which collapsed twice and is now drying on the windowsill.

qa.q: What does Dolma's line "That's new" show about how she feels?
qa.a: She is quietly proud and surprised that she went two hours without checking her phone, a sign she feels more secure.

qa.q: What else could keep Dolma's progress going?
qa.a: Continuing her counsellor sessions and her classes with friends like Tsering, and telling Sahil when the tight chest comes back instead of hiding it.

qa.q: How is Sahil helping trust grow from his side?
qa.a: He shares his day openly without being asked and calls when he says he will, so Dolma can rely on him.

grounding: It shows a young woman building her own worth through friends, a hobby and counselling while her partner stays open and steady.

passage:
Late that night, Sonali texted her boyfriend.
Sonali: saurabh, can I tell you something weird
Saurabh: always
Sonali: I felt that jealous twist today when you mentioned Ritika. even after you told me all about the lunch 😕
Saurabh: thanks for telling me. anything you want to ask?
Sonali: no, you've been really open. that's kind of the point. it keeps coming back even when you do everything right
Saurabh: hmm. what do you want to do about it?
Sonali: I booked a session with the counsellor at college. also joining the Thursday running group with Mehak
Saurabh: that sounds really good. I'm proud of you ❤️
Sonali: I'll still tell you when it hits, okay?
Saurabh: yes please. I'm not going anywhere
Sonali: 🙂

qa.q: Who is Sonali joining the Thursday running group with?
qa.a: She is joining it with Mehak.

qa.q: Why did Sonali decide to book a counsellor session?
qa.a: She noticed the jealousy keeps coming back even though Saurabh has been open, so she wants help working on it herself.

qa.q: What does this chat get right at this stage?
qa.a: Sonali names the feeling without blaming Saurabh and takes steps for herself, while Saurabh stays open and supportive; trust is growing from both sides.

qa.q: How might Saurabh feel reading Sonali's messages?
qa.a: He probably feels trusted and relieved that she tells him honestly, and wants to keep being steady for her.

grounding: It illustrates a young woman seeking counselling and building her own life when jealousy persists despite reassurance, while her partner stays open.

passage:
In the small town of Deoband, Rabia had spent a year being jealous of every woman Yusuf spoke to at his father's shop. She hated the feeling. It made her small.

This winter she did something about it. She joined the women's calligraphy class at the madrasa hall, something she had loved as a girl and let go. On Thursdays she went for walks with her cousin Chaitanya's wife, laughing about everything. When the jealousy still came back hard, she went twice to the counsellor at the district hospital.

Yusuf did his part. He told her who he'd be meeting and came home when he said. He didn't sigh when she asked a question.

One evening she saw him chatting with a customer, a young woman, and waited for the old burn in her chest. It came, but smaller. She picked up her pen and finished the letter she was inking.

qa.q: What class did Rabia join?
qa.a: The women's calligraphy class at the madrasa hall.

qa.q: How did Rabia feel when she saw Yusuf chatting with the young customer?
qa.a: She felt a small burn of jealousy, much weaker than before, and stayed calm enough to keep inking.

qa.q: What helped Rabia build inner security?
qa.a: Her own interests, time with friends and family, the counsellor when the jealousy came back hard, and Yusuf being open and consistent.

qa.q: How might Yusuf feel as Rabia grows more secure?
qa.a: He may feel relieved and trusted, glad that his openness and her own work are both paying off.

grounding: Rabia works on her own worth through calligraphy, friendship and a counsellor, while Yusuf stays open and consistent, so trust grows from both.

passage:
Freya had spent last spring checking Emre's phone in their Berlin flat, and hating herself for it.

This autumn things were different. She'd started climbing on Tuesdays with her friend Elif, and was, to her surprise, good at it. She'd picked her cello back up. And when the jealousy spiked badly in September, she had booked a few sessions with a counsellor at the student centre instead of waiting it out.

Emre had changed too. He told her about his plans without being asked. He left his phone on the table and didn't flinch when she walked past it.

On Saturday he went to a colleague's birthday. Freya felt the familiar tug of worry. Then she texted Elif: "Climbing tomorrow?" and practised a hard piece until her fingers ached.

When Emre came home, she realised she hadn't checked the time once.

qa.q: What did Freya start doing on Tuesdays?
qa.a: Climbing, with her friend Elif.

qa.q: How did Freya handle the tug of worry on Saturday?
qa.a: She felt the old worry but stayed steady, texting Elif and practising cello rather than checking on Emre.

qa.q: What role did the counsellor play in Freya's progress?
qa.a: When the jealousy spiked badly despite reassurance, the counsellor gave Freya support to work on it rather than waiting it out.

qa.q: What is it like for Emre when Freya no longer checks?
qa.a: He likely feels trusted and relieved, and more relaxed about being open.

grounding: Freya builds her own security through friends, climbing, cello and a counsellor, while Emre is open and consistent, so trust grows from both sides.

passage:
The student counselling centre at the university in Pune had a wall of paper cranes folded by past visitors. Trisha added one on her last session.

For three months she had come every Wednesday. At first she had talked only about Naveen: the girls he texted, the parties. Slowly the counsellor had turned the questions toward her. What did she enjoy? Who were her people?

Trisha had rejoined the debate club. She'd started cooking on Sundays with her flatmates. She'd noticed that the jealousy was loudest when she felt useless.

Naveen had come to one session too. He'd agreed to keep telling her his plans, not because he had to, but because it helped both of them.

"How is the jealousy now?" the counsellor asked.

"Still there some days," Trisha said. "But it doesn't drive the car anymore. I do."

qa.q: What was on the wall of the counselling centre?
qa.a: A wall of paper cranes folded by past visitors.

qa.q: How does Trisha feel about the jealousy now?
qa.a: She feels steadier and more in control; it still comes some days but no longer drives her.

qa.q: What combination helped Trisha build inner security?
qa.a: Counselling sessions, rejoining the debate club, cooking with flatmates, and Naveen's willingness to keep telling her his plans.

qa.q: How might Naveen see the change in Trisha?
qa.a: He may feel relieved and closer to her, glad that trust is now coming from both of them.

grounding: At a counselling centre Trisha builds inner security through friends, interests and support, while Naveen stays open, so trust grows from both.

passage:
Santosh,
It's been a year, and I wanted to write this down instead of saying it badly over dinner.
Six months ago I was the girlfriend who counted your replies. You never once made me feel foolish for it. You kept telling me where you were before I asked, and you introduced me to everyone at your office party, which I know you did on purpose.
But your openness couldn't fix the part of me that felt not enough. That part I had to work on myself. The Thursday sessions with the college counsellor helped more than I expected. So did pottery on Sundays, and getting back in touch with Shalu and the old hostel group.
Last week you went on the office trip and I didn't check anything. I just missed you. That felt new, and good.
Ira

qa.q: What does Ira do on Sundays now?
qa.a: Ira does pottery on Sundays.

qa.q: How did Ira feel during Santosh's office trip last week?
qa.a: Ira felt secure enough not to check anything and simply missed Santosh, which felt new and calm.

qa.q: Which steps helped Ira build inner security?
qa.a: Thursday sessions with the college counsellor, pottery, and reconnecting with Shalu and the hostel group, alongside Santosh being open and consistent.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Santosh during the months when Ira counted replies?
qa.a: Santosh may have felt watched at times, yet chose patience, sharing plans before being asked and including Ira at the office party.

grounding: Shows a young woman building her own worth through friends, interests and a counsellor while her partner stays open and consistent.
